turns.t: Morning. I'll not keep you long. I've still got this chest, and I thought it would have gone by now.
It's no bother, take your time. What's it been like? ~
I've had it nearly two weeks. I had a course from the walk-in centre, finished it on Sunday, and I'm no better, really.
What are you noticing? Cough, or breathlessness, or both?
A cough, mainly. Wet, and I'm bringing up green phlegm in the mornings. Most of the day, really.
How much, would you say, a spoonful, more?
A couple of spoonfuls in the morning, less in the day.
And your breathing?
Breathless on the stairs. I stop halfway up at work, and I never used to.
Does anything make it worse, lying down, cold air? ~
Not that I've noticed. It's worse when I get a coughing fit. ~
Do you smoke?
About ten a day. I know, I know.
Tell you what, I won't lecture you today, but I'll bring it up again, if that's all right. ~
Fair enough. ~
Take a deep breath in for me, through your mouth. I'll listen to your back. ~
Right. ~
And out. Again.
Is it bad? ~
I can hear some crackles at the bottom of the right lung, and a bit of wheeze on the left.
Is that pneumonia? ~
I'm not going to jump to a label yet. It tells me there's still some infection or inflammation down there. ~
What do we do? I thought the tablets would sort it. ~
Sometimes a chest takes longer to settle than the course lasts, especially in a smoker. I'd like you to give it a few more days. ~
And if it's not better? ~
If it's not better in a week, I'd want a chest X-ray to see what's going on in the lung.
A week. Right. ~
Keep drinking lots of fluids, and try not to suppress the cough at night, you want to clear it.
Should I stay off work? ~
Only if you feel you need to. Rest when you can. ~
Right. I'll see how I go. ~
And come in sooner if you cough up blood, get a high temperature, or get much more breathless.
I will, doctor. Thanks. ~
Take care. ~

physical_examination.finding: crackles at the bottom of the right lung
bit of wheeze on the left
